distractors.reason: We don't say 'do your hands'. 'Do' is used with tasks such as do homework or do the dishes.
We don't say 'make your hands'. 'Make' is used with things we create, such as make a cake or make a plan.
We don't say 'take your hands'. 'Take' is used with actions such as take a shower or take a break.

l1_interference: Em português usamos 'lavar' para as mãos, mas o aluno pode traduzir mal e escrever 'do' ou 'make'. Em inglês, use sempre 'wash' com 'hands'.
explanation: In English, 'wash' is the verb used with cleaning parts of the body such as your hands, your face or your hair.

related_collocations.example: I brush my teeth every morning.
Wash your face before you go to bed.
She washes her hair on Sunday.

memory_tip: WASH = clean a part of your body (hands, face, hair) | BRUSH = clean your teeth
